(i) earthquake occurrence in the Lower Rhine area can be well described by the ETAS model, and that (ii) the hazard is significantly underestimated when the temporal correlations between earthquakes are neglected.
(i) earthquake clustering can significantly impact the seismic hazard and (ii) the impact of clustering on seismic hazard can be quantified by using the ETAS model.

the time-dependent earthquake activity can have a significant impact on the seismic hazard, especially in low-seismicity regions.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the time dependence of earthquake occurrence can have a significant impact on the seismic hazard in low seismicity areas.
the time dependence of earthquake occurrence has to be taken into account in seismic hazard assessment in regions of moderate to low seismicity, where the number of earthquakes is limited.
the inclusion of the temporal correlation of earthquakes can significantly affect seismic hazard estimations, even in low‐seismicity regions.
